thread:
Maya (Product): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — clarification on how quotas and credits behave during deploy windows. Specifics: rolling canaries, failover to fallback models, and database migrations that spike tokens. Anyone from billing/infra able to confirm current policy? /cc @Ravi

Ravi (Finance): Short answer: usage is billed as observed. But we have some manual levers for one-off adjustments. Need specifics (times, org, estimate).

Jude (Eng): For rolling canaries we usually route small % to canary model. If canary model has higher per-token cost, you'll see higher spend. Quotas aren't automatically relaxed during deploys.

Maya (Product): So no auto-burst? What about scheduled deploys where we expect 3x traffic for ~10 mins — is there a grace policy?

Ravi (Finance): We do not have an automatic grace burst. We can do discretionary credit overrides or temporary quota bump on dedicated customers with a support ticket. For hosted customers, suggest pre-purchasing burst credits or contacting support 48h prior.

Sam (CEO): To add — long-term we want to automate short-lived burst allowances with guardrails. But today it's manual. Prioritize safety: automatic bursts must not allow runaway spend.

Jude (Eng): Also note: during canary -> fallback if canary fails, routing switches back quickly which can double-request patterns if clients retry. Best practice: clients should honor 429s and exponential backoff.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: service/api v1.23.4 -> canary 5% at 15:40 UTC

Olivia (SRE): Quick ops note — if you expect deploy-induced spikes, create a 'deploy-ops' runbook and add capacity requests in the runbook. We can tag runs for expedited quota review.

Maya (Product): Is there any way to get automated alerts when we're within 10% of quota so product teams know to pause deploys?

Ravi (Finance): We have alerts but they're at account level. Can configure route-level alerts in Console today (cost thresholds). I'll follow up to expose a 'pre-deploy' alert threshold.

Jude (Eng): Also watch caching — prefix caching reduces token spend during deploys. If you can freeze prompt churn during canary, that helps.

Sam (CEO): Action items: (1) Ravi to propose a "deploy burst" policy and SLAs for manual bump, (2) Eng to add a Console toggle for pre-deploy alerting, (3) Product to document best practices. Revisit in 2 weeks. :+1:

Ravi (Finance): I'll post a short FAQ for engineering playbooks.

Maya (Product): thanks — please @me on the doc. Also could we add an example snippet for the Console alert rule? like:

Jude (Eng): ```
# example pseudo
alert.when(cost_last_10m > expected_baseline*2)
notify(["#deploy-ops","owner@example.com"]) 
```

Olivia (SRE): noted. Also: if you expect DB migration to generate background jobs calling inference, schedule them off-peak or use a batch window to avoid hitting live quotas.

Maya (Product): perfect. That covers my questions for now.

Sam (CEO): Thanks all. We'll loop back with a short policy doc and a support flow.

Ravi (Finance): Filed internal ticket FIN-834: deploy-burst-policy - I'll update this thread when draft ready.

Maya (Product): appreciated :heart:
